**Step 1 - Scene:** A snack, not a full meal. It's a pile of whole roasted or raw almonds on a white square plate.

**Step 2 - Vessel:** A white square plate about 26 cm across (dinner-plate size). The almonds are about 2.5-3 cm long, so roughly 9-10 would fit across the plate. Plate area is about 600 cm² with the rounded corners.

**Step 3 - Items:** Almonds only. No oil, sauce, or other visible food.

**Step 4 - Area:** The almonds cover roughly 45% of the plate, about 270 cm². Plate is visible between many pieces.

**Step 5 - Height:** Mostly a single loose layer with some pieces resting on others and plate showing between them, so "flat" to "layer." I use about 1 cm.

**Step 6 - Volume and grams:** 270 cm² × 1 cm = 270 ml. Whole almonds have a bulk density of about 0.5 g/ml, so 270 × 0.5 ≈ 135 g. Counting about 70 almonds at roughly 1.2-1.4 g each gives about 85-100 g, so I take a value of about 100 g as the better estimate.

**Step 7 - Energy:** Almonds are about 579 kcal per 100 g. 100 g × 5.79 ≈ 580 kcal.

**Step 8 - Check:** Roughly 70 almonds on a dinner plate is a light snack, so about 100 g and about 580 kcal is plausible. It is not a heavy plate.
